skills.name: Data capture technologies: automatic input devices

note.text:
Data capture means getting data into a computer system. Automatic (direct) methods are fast and reduce typing errors:
• Barcode reader: reads product codes at supermarket tills. • QR code: square code read by phone cameras (payments, links).
• OCR (optical character recognition): turns scanned printed text into editable text. • OMR (optical mark recognition): reads pencil marks on multiple-choice answer sheets and forms.
• MICR (magnetic ink character recognition): reads the numbers printed in magnetic ink on cheques.
• Magnetic stripe and chip cards (with PIN): bank and ID cards. • RFID: radio tags read without contact (tickets, livestock, toll cards).
• Biometrics: fingerprints, face or iris to identify people. • Sensors: temperature, light, pressure for automatic monitoring.

sections.heading: Getting data in automatically
sections.text:
Typing data by hand is slow and causes mistakes. Data capture technologies read data straight into the computer.
• Barcode readers scan the striped codes on products at supermarket tills.
• QR codes are square patterns read by phone cameras, used for mobile payments and links.
• Magnetic stripe and chip cards (with a PIN) are used by banks and for ID.

sections.heading: Reading paper
sections.text:
• OMR (optical mark recognition) detects where pencil marks are on a form: multiple-choice answer sheets, lottery tickets, surveys.
• OCR (optical character recognition) turns scanned printed text into text you can edit.
• MICR (magnetic ink character recognition) reads the special numbers on cheques, printed in magnetic ink that is hard to forge.

sections.heading: Radio, bodies and sensors
sections.text:
• RFID (radio frequency identification) reads tags without contact: transport cards, library books, livestock ear tags, toll gates.
• Biometrics identify people by fingerprint, face or iris: phone unlocking, staff attendance, ID cards.
• Sensors measure temperature, light, pressure or movement automatically.
Choose the method that is fastest and most accurate for the job, and protect any personal data collected.

worked_example.problem: Which data capture method is best for marking {2000} multiple-choice answer sheets for a mock exam, and why?
steps: The pupils shade boxes with a pencil.
OMR reads the position of the marks automatically.
It is fast and accurate for large numbers of sheets.

cards.idea: Barcodes and QR codes are read by scanners or cameras.
OMR reads marks; OCR reads printed characters.
example: Exam answer sheets: OMR. Scanned letters: OCR.

example: Scanning a barcode beats typing a {13}-digit number.

pick.q: Why is scanning barcodes better than typing product codes at a till?
pick.r: It is faster and reduces typing errors
e: A computer looks up the price.
pick.y: Automatic capture is quick and accurate.

pick.q: Which is a disadvantage of biometric attendance systems?
pick.r: They store personal data that must be protected and can fail with dirty or injured fingers
w: They are always slower than paper
pick.y: Privacy and reliability must be considered.

pick.q: Why do banks use chip-and-PIN cards instead of only magnetic stripes?
pick.r: The chip is harder to copy, and the PIN proves the user
e: Cards do not hold money physically.
